insights.headline: MCX gold and silver held Monday's 2% rebound as Trump kept Iran strikes on the table
insights.summary: MCX December gold futures rose 2.38% to Rs 1,24,677 per 10 grams and silver 2.45% to Rs 1,51,435 per kg on Monday, holding the rebound from last week's slide to a 14-month low. Spot gold traded near $3,615 after Friday's lows briefly tested $3,500, while Trump said he favours resuming military action against Iran after the new year if talks fail. MCX closes its morning session on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti and reopens in the evening; traders now watch US core PCE on Wednesday.
points: MCX gold +2.38% to Rs 1,24,677 per 10 g; silver +2.45% to Rs 1,51,435 per kg.
Spot gold near $3,615 after Friday's lows briefly tested $3,500; silver near $42.18.
Trump is inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the new year if talks fail.
MCX morning session closed on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti; evening trading from 5 pm.
Next test: US core PCE on Wednesday at 19:00 IST, ahead of the Fed's 9 December decision.

brief.headline: Gold, silver rebound after worst week in 8 months
brief.summary: MCX gold rose 2.38% to Rs 1,24,677 per 10 g and silver 2.45% to Rs 1,51,435 per kg as Fed hike bets cooled.

bullets.text: An AI-led equity slide pushed traders toward havens, cooling December hike bets as liquidation eased, Mint and InvestingLive report.
Fresh positions built on MCX as the rebound gathered pace, and jewellers scaled back making-charge offers as prices eased.
Watch Wednesday: US core PCE at 19:00 IST, the next test for gold ahead of US jobs on 4 December and the Fed's 9 December decision.

trending.title: Gold and silver rebound on MCX after worst week since March
trending.summary: Spot gold rose 2.3% to $3,619 and MCX gold 2.38% to Rs 1,24,677 as dip-buyers returned and traders pared December Fed hike bets after an AI-led equity slide pushed money toward havens.

trending.title: Forced selling, not just rates, drove the 9% slide
trending.summary: Goldman Sachs' trading desk says speculative funds sold $9.3bn of gold in a week as AI-led equity losses forced margin calls, cutting net longs to about $72bn.

trending.title: Trump keeps Iran strikes on the table as gold rebounds
trending.summary: Trump told Fox News he is inclined to resume strikes on Iran if talks fail, and warned tankers testing the blockade would be sunk, keeping geopolitical risk live as bullion recovers.

trending.title: Silver's slide runs deeper than gold's
trending.summary: Silver fell 16.2% last week, deeper than gold's slide, then rebounded 2.5% to $42.18; Morgan Stanley still sees $71.40 while cheaper silver revived Salem's anklet makers.

trending.title: Asian demand splits: China buys record gold, India's imports fall
trending.summary: China imported a record $209bn of gold in Jan-Oct and its central bank added gold for a 24th month, while India's gold imports fell nearly 40% in Apr-Oct after the duty rose to 15% in May.

items.summary: MCX December gold futures rose Rs 2,899, or 2.38%, to Rs 1,24,677 per 10 grams as speculators built fresh positions on firm spot demand, PTI reported; silver futures gained 2.45% to Rs 1,51,435 per kg. In New York, gold futures rose 2.14% to $3,614.25 an ounce and silver futures 2.91%.
items.title: Gold futures rise to Rs 1.24 lakh per 10 grams, silver crosses Rs 1.51 lakh per kg

items.summary: MCX gold futures rose 2.2% and silver 2.11% on Monday after last week's slide — gold fell 11% and silver 16.2% on the week — as short covering and bargain buying met a softer dollar and fading bets on Fed hikes. Spot gold traded near $3,609, up 2%, and silver just above $42. Analysts quoted remain cautious, saying the rebound must hold above resistance to confirm a turn.
items.title: Gold and silver rebound over 2% after steep weekly losses: Can the recovery sustain?
Gold rebounds after biggest weekly drop in eight months as buyers return
items.summary: Gold rose as much as 2.6% to above $3,630 an ounce after a 9% weekly fall to a 14-month low, as dip-buyers stepped in and traders pared bets on a December Fed rate hike. Silver rose 2.5% to $42.18 after tumbling 15% last week. Retail buyers crowded gold shops in Shenzhen's Shuibei market, and a Friday Treasury rally on AI-spending worries plus a softer dollar aided the rebound.

items.title: Gold Rebounds as Tech Rout Spurs Shift to Havens, Treasury Rally
items.summary: Gold rebounded as much as 2.6% to around $3,630 an ounce after falling 9% last week to a 14-month low, as a rout in technology shares pushed traders toward havens and pulled down Treasury yields and the dollar. Spot gold was up 1.4% at $3,587.13 in Singapore, while silver rose 1.9% to $41.92 after tumbling 15% the week before.

Gold's rebound has not cleared the risks hanging over the metal, Investing.com's analysis says, with hawkish Fed expectations and fragile sentiment still in play after last week's 9% slide. Traders now look to Wednesday's US core PCE data for the next steer on interest rates.
items.title: Gold Recovers Ground, but the Bulls Aren't Out of the Woods Yet

items.summary: Gold's worst week in eight months was driven less by rates alone than by forced selling, analysts say: as AI-led equities slid, leveraged investors sold gold to meet margin calls. Goldman Sachs' trading desk estimates speculative funds sold $9.3bn in a week, cutting net longs to about $72bn. Goldman now sees gold at $4,150 by end-2026 and $4,650 by end-2027.
items.title: Gold sinks 9% in a week as margin calls and Fed hike bets override its haven role
Gold Rebound Faces Pressure as Trump Keeps Military Action Against Iran on Table
items.summary: Gold's rebound faces fresh pressure after Donald Trump said he favours resuming military action against Iran after the new year if no agreement is reached, keeping the threat of renewed strikes in focus even as bullion recovers from a 14-month low. Trump also warned tankers testing the US blockade of Iranian oil would be sunk.

items.title: Gold Is Rebounding, but Why Are Buyers Still Cautious?
items.summary: Gold traded near $3,615, above Friday's lows that briefly tested $3,500, but DailyForex cautions the rebound is fragile: a strong dollar, heavy speculative short positioning and a Thanksgiving trading slowdown cloud the outlook, and the metal has yet to show buyers returning in force.

items.title: Gold in a free fall: Why November 25, December 4 and 9 could be crucial for prices
items.summary: Gold faces three decisive US events in the coming weeks, Upstox notes: October PCE inflation data on November 25, the US jobs report on December 4, and the Fed's policy decision on December 9. Bullion has fallen nearly 30% from its January record highs, with Indian gold at a one-year low after nine straight sessions of declines, as a stronger dollar, high Treasury yields and Fed hike bets weigh.

items.title: Stock market holiday tomorrow Tuesday, 24 Nov: BSE, NSE open or closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti? Check exchange calendar
items.summary: Indian stock markets stay shut on Tuesday, 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti. MCX closes its morning session but reopens for the evening session from 5 pm, when gold and silver futures can trade; 24 November is also a settlement holiday.

items.title: Indian rupee could rise to 91.50/$ on equity inflows, HDFC Bank's treasury head says
items.summary: The rupee could strengthen to 91.50 per dollar if strong equity inflows continue, HDFC Bank treasury head Arup Rakshit said, seeing it in a 91.50-93.50 range near term. The currency closed Friday at 92.67, up nearly 2.5% in November on record $12 billion of foreign equity inflows, and Rakshit expects the RBI to raise rates in December, with a 25-basis-point hike more or less given.

China imported a record $209 billion of gold in the first ten months of 2026, nearly 8% of all imports, tempering a trade surplus that has passed $1 trillion. Brad Setser of the Council on Foreign Relations estimates the full-year surplus would reach $1.5 trillion without gold, against about $1.3 trillion with it.
items.title: China's Record Gold Imports Partially Mask Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus
China Gold Reserves Rise for a 24th Month as the Price Falls
items.summary: China's central bank added about 26 tonnes of gold in October, its largest buy in three years, taking reserves to 78.3 million ounces in a 24th straight monthly rise even as bullion fell. The World Gold Council puts central-bank buying at 321 tonnes in Q3, but only 228 tonnes of the 675-tonne nine-month total was publicly reported. Poland held 673 tonnes at end-September against a 700-tonne goal.

items.title: Silver Price Just Lost 16% In A Week. Morgan Stanley Still Sees $71.40
items.summary: Silver closed Friday at $41.00 an ounce, down 16% in a week. Morgan Stanley still sees $71.40 by the second quarter of 2027, about 74% above Friday's close, though it expects silver to lag gold on weak industrial demand. Goldman Sachs sees little chance of another London squeeze in 2027.

items.title: Silver price dip revives Salem's anklet industry
items.summary: Salem's silver anklet makers are seeing orders return as silver eased to about Rs 175 a gram from Rs 195 a week earlier, after the January peak of nearly Rs 425 a gram. Units are now getting about a lakh anklet orders a month, roughly half their normal volume, ahead of Pongal.

items.title: Did PM Modi's appeal really bring down gold prices? Here's what the data shows
items.summary: Mathrubhumi tests the PM's claim that his appeal to avoid non-essential gold purchases lowered prices: 24-carat gold fell about 18% from Rs 15,250 a gram on 9 May to Rs 12,523 on 21 November. The piece concludes the appeal alone cannot explain it — the import duty rose from 6% to 15% in May, imports fell about 40% in April–October, and a stronger dollar and Fed hike expectations also weighed.

items.title: PM Modi's appeal to avoid gold purchases reflects in import data, India saves $16.46 billion in 7 months: CAIT
items.summary: India's gold import bill fell nearly 40% to $24.78 billion in April–October 2026 from $41.24 billion a year earlier, saving $16.46 billion, the Confederation of All India Traders says, crediting PM Modi's appeal to avoid non-essential gold purchases. October imports fell 62.6% to $5.51 billion from $14.72 billion a year earlier.

items.title: As gold price ease, jewellers scale back offers, making-charge discounts
items.summary: Pune jewellers are cutting back the making-charge discounts they offered when gold was soaring, reverting charges to original levels as prices ease to about Rs 1.23 lakh per 10 g. Demand is returning for weddings and gifting, but buyers favour lightweight designs and smaller pieces.

items.title: IBJA Seeks BIS Crackdown on Fake Purity Reports and 4,000 Unregistered Gold Refiners
items.summary: The India Bullion and Jewellers Association has asked the Bureau of Indian Standards to act on alleged collusion between jewellers and hallmarking centres, fake purity reports and rhenium adulteration, and to bring nearly 4,000 unregistered refiners under oversight. BIS has called a meeting on November 23 to examine the complaints.

items.title: 121 kg of gold: Anonymous devotee to make biggest-ever individual offering to Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala on Nov 26
items.summary: An anonymous devotee will hand over 121 kg of gold ornaments — 45 pieces in nine sets, valued at about Rs 160 crore — to Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala on 26 November, in what temple sources describe as the largest individual offering in the shrine's history.
